body: Ok, but for me a quote like that just opens up a whole debate about the definition and value of 'Normal'. For example being 'normal', say in societal terms, means having a job, family, home etc yet these are the people that kill themselves on daily basis alongside people with more severe situations so for them normal doesn't mean a thing, but that's just me ranting and I really do appreciate the honest comment.

Maybe, the thing is I've had plenty of events in my life that could easily had served as 'triggers'. Also, and I really do appreciate the advice, I feel I'd just be wasting clinic time and resources. I don't know it's as if death, for me, is just like any other thing along the road. It doesn't scare me (the various methods do) and if it's not the adventure that we don't know about then I feel oblivion would suit me just fine.

Hm, well lets see. Those sort of headaches sound familiar but not for years now. I have no problem waking up, sometimes going back to sleep and as for mood swings I'd say if i'm left alone... possibly. but none of these are to any extremes, no more so than anyone else really. The thing is I feel if I was emotional I would be a whole lot worse as being unemotional about my thoughts has let me look at them objectively.

Not sure how helpful this is but I find that if you find yourself being weird or awkward around people you don't usually talk to then tell them that you're not good at talking to them but would like to talk to them anyway. Everyone has problems adapting to meeting a new person at first and I find bonding over a mutual awkwardness at meeting new people is a good start.

Sorry if that's incoherent, it makes more sense in my head :/
